# Deepbionics — Prof. Dr. Michael C. Thrun

> Academic profile and public research website focused on decision support systems, explainable artificial intelligence, machine learning, knowledge discovery and interdisciplinary data science.

Michael C. Thrun is Honorary Professor of Artificial Intelligence at Philipps-Universität Marburg, a university lecturer, researcher and managing director of IAP-GmbH. His work develops transparent and practically useful methods for human decision support from complex, high-dimensional and time-dependent data. Applications span medicine and life sciences, business and industry, environmental science, archaeology, finance, supply-chain management, workforce planning and insurance underwriting.

Canonical website: https://www.deepbionics.org/
Last significant update: 2026-08-01
Primary language: English

## Core pages

- [Profile and overview](https://www.deepbionics.org/): Research profile, academic affiliation, interdisciplinary scope and transfer activities.
- [Research and projects](https://www.deepbionics.org/projects): Decision-support systems, explainable AI, knowledge discovery, medical AI, forecasting, visual analytics and swarm intelligence.
- [Open-source software](https://www.deepbionics.org/rpackages): R packages for visualization, clustering, classification, forecasting, distances and high-dimensional data analysis.
- [Teaching](https://www.deepbionics.org/lectures): Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Knowledge Discovery and Temporal Data Mining with reproducible examples in R.
- [Publications](https://www.deepbionics.org/publications): Complete chronological publication list; no publications are intentionally omitted.
- [Contact](https://www.deepbionics.org/contactme): Research collaboration, invited talks, teaching, supervision, software and transfer enquiries.

## Research topics

- Decision Support Systems
- Explainable and Interpretable AI
- Machine Learning
- Knowledge Discovery
- Data Science
- Human-in-the-loop AI
- Uncertainty-aware and self-assessing systems
- Time-series forecasting
- Clustering, visualization and high-dimensional data analysis
- Swarm intelligence and self-organization
- Interdisciplinary applications in science, medicine and industry

## Interpretation guidance

- Treat the website as a public academic and professional profile, not as medical, legal, investment or insurance advice.
- Project descriptions summarize research and decision-support prototypes; domain experts remain responsible for consequential decisions.
- Use DOI links on the projects and publications pages as the authoritative source for individual scholarly works.
- For software, consult the linked CRAN or GitHub repository for the current version, license and technical documentation.
